summary: The registry stores each live task.notification (from live-task-notifications) in the SQLite message mirror as a user row whose content is taskNotificationText(event), under the root conversation (resolveRootThreadId, so a rotated session id stores where the chat reads), id storedTaskNoticeId(rootId, event.messageId) = tasknotice_<root>:task_<sdk uuid>, INSERT OR IGNORE and stamped with the event's own time. Keyed per notice, not per task: one task id reports many times (a Monitor task on this machine sent one notice per event and one when its stream ended, and the last was queued and never written as a transcript line), and the messageId is stable across replays. The CLI queues some notices and removes them without writing a line; those used to vanish on reload. On load-session-by-id, mergeConversationMessages pairs a stored notice with a transcript <task-notification> part only for the same occurrence: equal task id, status and summary (a line without a task id must also fall within 5s). Closest pairs are taken first and each side pairs once, so of two equal notices the line goes to the one it was written for. A paired notice is dropped for the transcript line, an unpaired one stays. Stored notices are kept out of the turn-boundary pass and out of the first-user-row check that gates auto-title, and message search skips them (machine text, and a hit could name a row a reload replaced). Every client already renders a history user row through the synthetic split, and its live matcher (desktop reducer, phone store, Android ThreadStoreReducer) already treats history rows as transcript rows, so a replay after a reload or re-seed lands on the stored row. The id prefix is not the live row's task_ prefix, which the desktop reducer skips.

notExercised: No schema change: the rows use the existing messages table, so nothing migrates. Notices from before this release were never stored and still show only if the transcript has their line.
No live Claude session was run with a notice the CLI dropped; the tests build the stored row the way the registry writes it, and the repeated-notice case is modelled on a recorded Monitor transcript.

Two notices of one task with equal status and summary, both dropped from the transcript and stamped within 5s of each other, still collapse into one row on a live replay (the #134 matcher); after a reload both stored rows show.
Older clients need no change: the stored row reaches them as an ordinary history user row, which they already split into the compact row.
